clues: Plaster forensic cast of a boot impression taken at the farmhouse rear entrance — tread pattern matches size 10.5 Canadian Forces parade boots recovered from Williams's Tweed residence.
Isolated 1920s limestone farmhouse, Highway 37, Hastings County — victim's residence and primary scene. Remote location; multiple unforced entry points documented.
Dark mahogany wooden box with brass hasp lock, recovered under floorboards of Williams's Tweed property — contents include personal articles traced to multiple victims.
Canadian Forces dark-blue colonel's beret with CFB Trenton insignia found in Williams's effects — his command visibility had initially appeared to rule him out.

runtimeCase.brief: On February 7, 2010, investigators questioned Colonel Russell Williams at Ottawa Police Service while the search for Jessica Lloyd was still active. Tire-track analysis, vehicle scrutiny, and inconsistencies in Williams's account had begun to collapse the image of a disciplined air-force commander into that of the prime suspect.
